summary.headline: Narayana Health Q1 FY27 call: India hospital EBITDA margin ~24% with footfalls up; insurance and UK losses weigh on consolidated margins.
summary.overview: Management said India hospital growth came from both volumes and realisations, helped by high-end and robotic procedures and clinic-driven footfalls. Insurance losses rose sharply in the quarter on a small book, though management said the July renewal cycle went through at 100% acceptance and Cayman insurance losses fell to about USD 3.7 million from USD 5.2 million quarter-on-quarter. UK business was hit by a severe heat wave and a longer software certification timeline, and it remains about 95% NHS by value. Management guided that margins should trend upward over the medium term but gave no numeric targets.

financial_highlights.change: Analyst cited 40% EBITDA growth; margin expansion stated as 400 bps YoY for India business net of clinic losses

financial_highlights.value: approx. INR 15 crore in Q1 FY27

financial_highlights.change: down from approx. USD 5.2 million in Q4 FY26 (QoQ)

financial_highlights.value: about 6% in USD terms (analyst figure, not disputed)
about 5% YoY growth on pre-acquisition comparable basis
INR 327 crore in Q1 FY27 vs INR 244 crore in Q4 FY26
financial_highlights.change: Q4 figure reflected a Cayman reclass; management said underlying cost flat QoQ

segments.name: India hospitals
segments.commentary: Growth from both ARPOB and footfalls, supported by high-end procedures, robotics and clinic referrals; no meaningful bed addition expected for 2-3 years. Management said margin expansion will continue, with the leverage benefit partly reinvested in integrated care.

segments.name: India clinics
segments.commentary: OP consultations about 66,000 in the quarter, up about 30% YoY; clinic footfall about 30% of hospital OPD footfall. Clinic losses about INR 15 crore in Q1 FY27; two more clinics opening this quarter.

segments.name: India insurance (Narayana Health Insurance)
segments.commentary: Loss ratio spiked in Q1 on a small book with a few large claims; expense ratio fell substantially. Management is focused on SME and retail, AI-led claims review, and in-housing claims; no numeric loss or breakeven guidance.

segments.name: Cayman hospitals
segments.commentary: Sequentially soft quarter, but management cited healthy double-digit YoY growth in discharges and OP footfall. Cayman margins back to earlier levels after ramp-up, per management.

segments.name: Cayman insurance
segments.commentary: Quarterly losses fell to about USD 3.7 million from about USD 5.2 million QoQ. July renewals had 100% acceptance; book about USD 60 million annualised.

segments.name: UK hospitals
segments.commentary: Acquired business was about 95% NHS by value, against a peer at about 70%; private share at an all-time high but still low. Heat wave disrupted chillers and HVAC; software certification adds about 4 to 6 months.

guidance_outlook: Management expects core operating margin to expand over time given leverage benefit, but declined to give a numeric projection.
Insurance book expected to moderate its loss ratio over time; management would not give a timeline for profitability.
Management said worst of Cayman insurance losses is behind on a rolling two-to-three-quarter basis, barring large-claim swings.
Management committed INR 3,000 crore of projects over the next two years, funded partly by internal cash and partly by borrowing.
Net debt to EBITDA expected to decline by FY30 after debt rises during the 2-3 year build-out.
capex_capacity: Southwest Bangalore project of about 100 beds: construction at end stage; start targeted by end of Q2 FY27.

Three projects slipped from FY28 to FY29 (two) and FY30 (one), mainly asset-light partner projects with licensing delays expected to clear in about a month; management said the slips are within the 6-month acceptable window.
No meaningful bed additions expected for the next 2-3 years.
North Bangalore expansion already announced for the first round; future expansion priority in Bangalore.
Expansion to new states such as UP and Bihar deferred until Phase 1 of capital deployment progresses.
demand_pricing: India hospital volume growth across all regions, alongside realisation gains; management declined to give volume or price numbers.
Analyst questioned the 24% EBITDA margin versus peers' lower ARPOB; management said further margin expansion is possible.
UK private revenue share at an all-time high but still very low versus peers; NHS dependence to fall over 4 to 5 years.
Cayman insurance renewals in July had 100% acceptance of repriced premiums; January cycle expected to be similar.
Management said it does not disclose the share of insurance-originated admissions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did India hospital footfalls rise alongside ARPOB, and is margin expansion still possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Venkatesh cited high-end and robotic procedures and clinic-driven brand strength (clinic footfall about 30% of OPD). Sandhya said margin expansion will continue because no beds are being added, but the split between cash flow and affordable pricing is an ongoing choice.

qa_highlights.question: Why did insurance losses spike and will they persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Ravi said the book is small, so a few large claims distort loss ratios; expense ratio fell substantially. Actions include AI-led claims review, in-housing claims, and a shift toward SME and retail, with no timeline for normalisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the UK ROCE and the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandhya said it is too early to measure and reporting may start in about four quarters. Anesh said there is no defined ROCE target.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Cayman hospital growth soft and when will Cayman insurance break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Anesh said Q1 is seasonally weak and volumes grew at a healthy double-digit rate YoY; insurance losses fell QoQ to about USD 3.7 million, and July renewals were fully accepted.

qa_highlights.question: Why did UK losses rise sequentially and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Anesh cited a severe heat wave that disrupted HVAC and chillers, and software certification taking 4 to 6 months longer than expected. Cost measures include standardising consumables and automating admin, with private payer mix still early.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the jump in professional fees to doctors QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandhya said Q4 included a reclass of Cayman doctor fees out of the professional fees line, so the Q4 base was distorted; underlying cost was flat.
